newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 30.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - January 30.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for REUTERS by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Pioneer
CONGRESS, SAMAJWADI PARTY COMING TOGETHER

The Congress Party and Samajwadi Party (SP) appeared to be coming together to break the political impasse in Uttar Pradesh (UP). Indications to this effect came when the SP president said the Congress should join hands with his party to form a government in UP. Congress leader in the lower house Sharad Pawar echoed the view. The development seemed to be the fallout of the strained relations between the Congress and the Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP). Sensing the danger, the BSP went on the defensive with their general secretary asserting that the alliance was intact. However, her statement was at variance with the BSP chief's assertion that the alliance was over.
The Times Of India
ESTIMATED $4 -11 BLN CAPITAL FLIGHT FROM INDIA

A research study has estimated the capital flight from India to the United States in 1994 and 1995 between $3.86 billion and $11.30 billion. The findings indicated there was nearly 20 percent under-invoicing of Indian imports from the U.S. while the extent of over-invoicing of exports was as high as 40 percent. Total Indo-U.S. trade in 1994 was $7.6 billion which rose to $9.03 billion in 1995. Considering that the U.S. accounted for about 20 percent of India's foreign trade, with other hard currency areas accounting for another 35 percent, total capital outflow in the two years may have been at least double the minimum estimated figures. This implied that India's trade gap was artificial
Indian Express
FIRE IN BOMBAY BUILDING KILLS THREE

The top four floors of the 25 storey Express Towers at Nariman Point in Bombay were gutted in a major fire that broke out on Wednesday morning. Three people, all employees of Pfeizer Limited, situated on the 22nd and 23rd floor, died of suffocation. The fire was believed to have started from the 21st floor occupied by Pfeizer and McKinsey, a leading consultancy company, which was renovating their offices.
The Economic Times
HIGHER THAN EXPECTED GDP GROWTH AT 6.7 PCT

The Economic Survey for fiscal 1996/97 (April-March) is set to estimate GDP growth at about 6.7 percent. This came about after the Central Statistical Organisation's upward revision of the 1995/96 growth rate to 7.1 percent. This was an improvement on the earlier expectation of the 1996/97 GDP growth rate slowing down to about 6 percent. Sources said the impressive growth in the service sector recorded in 1995/96 continued in 1996/97 and would largely neutralise the expected slowdown in the manufacturing sector. A TRUNCATED PACKAGE MAY SMOTHER HOPES

The Prime Minister's package to boost the capital market was likely to fall short of expectations. Finance Ministry officials, while admitting there would be some announcements, said they should be seen in the larger context of the reform of the capital market. A government spokesman said the package would address broader issues concerning the economy and not focus just on the stock market. Finance Ministry officials also clarified that no fiscal incentives relating to the capital market would be announced as these, if at all, would figure in the budget.
HOTEL INDUSTRY IN FOR A BONANZA

The Tourism Ministry has proposed including the tourism industry in the infrastructure sector in the budget. If the proposal was accepted by the Finance Ministry, hotel companies would get exemption from capital gains tax. Sources said the ministry was keen to ensure tourism was viewed as an industry bringing in investment and employment rather than an elitist activity. Formerly, the ministry held the view that while hotels badly needed investment for rapid development, the transportation sector did not need similar tax benefits as it was not very capital intensive. Financial Express
ICICI MAY FUND BPL-US WEST SANS GUARANTEE

The Industrial Credit and Investment Corporation of India (ICICI) is likely to finance the BPL-US West cellular phone service project without insisting on corporate guarantees. Whereas corporate guarantees were required for projects involving risks, ICICI was not adamant on making this a precondition to disburse funds to BPL-US West, an official said. Financial institutions, not yet familiar with telecom projects, were adopting a cautious approach for their funding, he added. ICICI was studying the technical and financial viability of the project as also the projections. If they were found satisfactory, ICICI would go ahead with funding the 15 percent rupee loan requirement of the 50 bil
Business Standard
WTO ALLOWS INDIA MORE TIME TO LIFT IMPORT CURBS

India has obtained a five-month reprieve for lifting the quantitative restrictions on imports. It successfully argued before the World Trade Organisation (WTO) committee in Geneva that there was still room for caution with regards to the country's balance of payments (BOP). Officials said the country came in for attack from the International Monetary Fund and the European Union for its stand. Negotiations would now be resumed afresh in the first week of June. Earlier India was required to set a timetable for withdrawing restrictions from April 1, 1997.
ADB TO EXTEND $1.3 BLN CREDIT LINE TO GUJARAT

The Asian Development Bank (ADB) cleared a direct line of credit estimated at $1.3 billion for Gujarat. This was the first instance of a multilateral agency extending a direct credit line to a state. The ADB credit line consists of a $1.0 billion package to revamp the state's infrastructure and an estimated $300 million to restructure state-owned firms in the state. The details of the $300 million package were finalised between ADB representatives and the Gujarat State Financial Corporation.
BHARAT RAM GROUP ADVISED TO FIND NEW CORE AREA

International management consultants McKinsey & Co have advised the Bharat Ram group to identify a new core area of business. Vivek Bharat Ram, a director on the board of SRF Ltd and part of the Bharat Ram family, was given the mandate to identify the new area. The move comes at a time when the Bharat Ram group has started to pull out of its traditional core areas like automobiles, financial services, ophthalmic lenses and polyester films. The group also decided not to appoint family members of the next generation to important board positions. RTZ-CRA TO INVEST $800M IN VENTURE WITH OMC

RTZ-CRA, world's largest mining group, will invest $800 million over the next three to four years in its joint venture with Orissa Mining Corporation (OMC). The venture was formed to develop two iron ore deposits in Orissa's Keonjhar-Singbhum region. RTZ-CRA holds a 51 percent stake in the project and the rest is held by OMC. The Anglo-American mining group was also close to finalising a joint venture with the Central India Coal Company for mining captive coal blocks. The group has also entered into a 50:50 agreement with the Tata group cement maker ACC for exploration of precious metals.
FDI PROPOSALS FOR FOREIGN AIRLINES TO BE SCREENED

The Civil Aviation Minister ruled out foreign airlines investing in domestic carriers even indirectly through a front company. The government would investigate this aspect of any foreign investment proposal, he said. The minister said Jet Airways would have to voluntarily divest its foreign equity and the ministry would act only if the domestic airline did not comply with the guideline. Jet Airways is owned by Tailswinds, an Isle-of-Man holding company. While a London-based non resident Indian holds a 60 percent stake in the holding company, Gulf Air and Kuwait Airways hold 20 percent each in the firm.
Business Line
GOVERNMENT PULLED UP ON LEVY SUGAR PRICE

In a judgment on an application by the Indian Sugar Mills Association, the apex court pulled up the government on the issue of levy sugar prices. The court observed the government was behaving like an ordinary litigant by trying to find excuses for not complying with its direction to refix the price of levy sugar. The court had ordered refixation of prices in September 1993, taking into account the additional cane price paid by the industry to farmers.
The Observer
WELFARE PACKAGE FOR RURAL POOR

Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda asked Finance Minister P. Chidambaram to accommodate a comprehensive welfare package for the rural poor in the forthcoming budget. The package consisted of jobs for at least one member of every rural poor family, a hike in family pension for rural unemployed and special relief, including housing, for agricultural labour.
